task.description: Implement the ISS-0480 remedy per the gate-approved design: revert test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs from async: true to async: false, rewrite their moduledoc async-justification sections to record the revert and why, and verify with (1) mix compile/format, (2) the two files' own tests, (3) design §4.1 static grep + §4.2 4+-seed empirical stress reproduction using Step 1's proven recipe with a real before/after comparison, (4) a full-suite run via scripts/test_parallel.sh.

result.summary:
IMPLEMENTED EXACTLY THE DESIGN'S TWO-LINE CHANGE, NO OTHER FILE TOUCHED. test/letflow/secrets_test.exs:31 and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs:36 changed from `use Letflow.DataCase, async: true` to `async: false`. Both moduledocs' `async: true (ISS-0113/ISS-0423 ...)` sections were rewritten in place to state: the file's own ISS-0113 three-mechanism classification was correct and is not retracted; ISS-0480 found a fourth, systemic mechanism (provisioned_tenant!/1's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call discards every other checked-out connection in the pool via DBConnection.Ownership.Manager's empty-except-list check-in, whenever the mode actually changes) that makes async:true unsafe for this file given any other concurrently-scheduled async:true test with an open checkout (which DataCase.setup/1 gives unconditionally); reverting to async:false removes the call from the async scheduling phase entirely, by construction; and a pointer to ISS-0480's design doc §6 for the longer-term fix. No lib/ file, no fixture file (tenant_fixture.ex/data_case.ex untouched, confirmed by final git status), and no test-body/assertion in either file changed.

===== VERIFICATION 1: COMPILE / FORMAT =====
`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, no output, no warnings.
`mix format --check-formatted test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs`: clean, no output (both already formatted).

===== VERIFICATION 2: THE TWO FILES' OWN TESTS =====
`mix test test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs` -- 38 passed (1 property, 37 tests), 0 failures, 57.7s (now fully sync as expected).

===== VERIFICATION 3: DESIGN SECTION 4.1 STATIC CHECK, LITERAL OUTPUT =====
Command run verbatim: `grep -rl "Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo\|Sandbox.mode(Repo" test --include=*.exs | xargs -I{} sh -c 'grep -m1 "^\s*use Letflow.DataCase" {} | sed "s|^|{}: |"'`.
Returned 76 rows (matches CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own independently-re-run count of 76, not the design's illustrative 75 -- already flagged by them as a non-blocking cosmetic miscount in the design's prose, not a defect). Every single row shows `async: false`, INCLUDING `test/letflow/secrets_test.exs: use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` and `test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs: use Letflow.DataCase, async: false`. ZERO rows show `async: true`. This is the exact postcondition Section 4.1 requires -- INV-1 holds by construction. Full 76-line output was inspected directly (not sampled); pasting the two previously-hazardous rows plus the zero-count confirmation here since the full 76-line dump is mechanical and identical in shape to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own already-recorded finding.

===== VERIFICATION 4: EMPIRICAL STRESS -- BEFORE/AFTER ON THE SAME HOST, SAME RECIPE =====
Recipe used, matching Step 1/design §4.2 exactly: `mix test $(grep -rl "async: true" test --include=*.exs) --seed <S>` (95 files by this looser grep both before and after -- the two culprit files' moduledoc prose still mentions the string "async: true" historically even after their `use` line flipped, which is harmless as an extra file argument per the design's own §0 note; their `use` declaration is what actually governs scheduling and is confirmed async:false by Verification 3).

BEFORE (unmodified branch tip, re-run by me on this host rather than relying solely on Step 1's numbers, to get a real same-host before/after pair) -- seed 1: FAILED. `Letflow.RowApprovalTest` "approving the same approver twice is idempotent" (test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs:30) -- `assert :ok = RowApproval.approve(id, :finance)` got `{:error, :not_found}` instead of `:ok`. This is the identical failure shape/mechanism Step 1's own diagnosis documented (a bystander async:true test's connection discarded mid-test by secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs's Sandbox.mode(:auto) flip). 3 total failures that run (RowApprovalTest, Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest, Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest); only RowApprovalTest is attributable to ISS-0480's mechanism, the other two are unrelated pre-existing flakes (TenantStatusTest not previously named by this issue; LintHandoffsTest is the already-filed ISS-0445). I did not run 3 more baseline seeds myself given this one already reproduced the named defect on this host under real conditions and Step 1 already established the 3/4 baseline rate rigorously -- burning further multi-hundred-second baseline runs against already-established evidence was judged not to add information proportional to its cost; flagged here for REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR rather than silently decided.

AFTER (with the two-line revert in place), 4 runs, 4 different seeds, all against the fix:
  - seed 1: 1752/1754 passed, 2 failures -- Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest, Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest (ISS-0445). ZERO in RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest.
  - seed 20260905: 1752/1754 passed, 2 failures -- Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest ("global isolation AC3"), Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest. ZERO in RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest.
  - seed 777: 1753/1754 passed, 1 failure -- Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest only. ZERO in RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest.
  - seed 424242: 1753/1754 passed, 1 failure -- Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest only. ZERO in RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest.

RESULT: 0/4 post-fix failures in either named test, against a same-host, same-recipe baseline that DID reproduce RowApprovalTest's failure on its very first attempt. This is the before/after comparison the task required, not a green-run-alone inference. PackUpdateMigrationTest did not fail in any of my 4 post-fix runs either, consistent with (not proof of) the design's §5 mechanism-level argument for covering it -- I did not reproduce it pre-fix either (matching Step 1's own 0/4), so this record carries forward the same honestly-disclosed asymmetry the design itself named: RowApprovalTest's coverage is empirically demonstrated by a real before/after pair; PackUpdateMigrationTest's is covered by mechanism argument only, not by direct repro on either side.

Unrelated failures observed across the 5 stress runs (1 baseline + 4 post-fix) -- TenantStatusTest (1x), Lua.ExecutorTest (1x), LintHandoffsTest (4x, ISS-0445) -- none reach Sandbox.mode/TenantFixture in a way relevant to this mechanism; not attributed to this change.

===== VERIFICATION 5: FULL SUITE (scripts/test_parallel.sh) =====
First attempt failed environmentally: 12 of 16 partitions aborted with DBConnection.ConnectionError / pool exhaustion during ecto.migrate setup, traced to stale `tenant_template_build_*` schemas and tenant_schemas rows left behind across ALL 16 test databases -- residue from tool-timeout-killed stress runs earlier in this same session (the sanctioned before/after runs above all completed cleanly; the contamination came from intermediate runs that got killed by the 10-minute tool-call cap mid-flight, matching this project's known ISS-0107-adjacent pattern). This is exactly the kind of misleading, non-code-related failure the task brief and Step 1's own handoff warned about -- not evidence about ISS-0480. Diagnosed via direct psql inspection (not assumed): every one of the 16 letflow_test<N> databases had 1-2 leftover `tenant_template_build_<hash>` schemas plus matching tenant_schemas rows; letflow_test1 additionally had a stray `tenant_template_refcheck` schema. Cleaned thoroughly (DROP SCHEMA CASCADE for every `tenant_template%`-prefixed schema plus matching tenant_schemas row deletion, across all 16 DBs, verified zero remaining afterward), then re-ran.

Second attempt, clean environment: `combined: 3225 tests, 6 properties, 4 failures (3227/3231 passed)`. All 4 failures identified and checked individually, none in RowApprovalTest/PackUpdateMigrationTest, none touching Sandbox.mode/TenantFixture: Mix.Tasks.Letflow.LintHandoffsTest (ISS-0445, already tracked), Letflow.SandboxPoolTest ("ISS-0224 regression" RT-8 death-path race, async:false, pre-existing named regression test for a different issue), Letflow.Scheduler.PollerTest x2 ("REQ-218 AC3" capacity-rejection timing tests, async:false). All three non-LintHandoffsTest files confirmed via grep to be async:false (cannot race the async cohort per ExUnit's own phase-separation guarantee) and to not reference Sandbox.mode/TenantFixture in a way relevant to this defect -- attributed to pre-existing flakiness in timing-sensitive scheduler/pool tests, not a regression from this change.

===== SELF-REVIEW PER AGENT INSTRUCTIONS =====
No state-transition/gen_statem code touched -- README.md state diagram not applicable. process_instance.ex not touched -- its property test unaffected. No migration added. mix compile/format run and confirmed clean, not claimed without running. No lib/ file, no fixture file changed -- confirmed by final `git status --short` showing only the two intended test files modified.

Probes cleaned up: all baseline/postfix/full-suite log files removed from the repo root, /tmp/letflow_test_parallel.* directories removed, tenant_template(+build) state cleaned across all 16 test DBs, no orphaned erl.exe processes left running (only the pre-existing, unrelated ElixirLS language-server erl.exe process, PID unchanged throughout this session, was ever present at rest).

issues.description: Did not personally re-run 3 additional pre-fix baseline seeds (only 1) before applying the fix, relying on Step 1's already-rigorous 3/4-of-4 baseline measurement for the remaining statistical weight, since my own seed-1 baseline attempt already reproduced the named RowApprovalTest failure on this host under real conditions. Judged proportionate given each full async-cohort run costs 550-700s and Step 1's baseline evidence was independently re-verified as sound by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR; flagged for REVIEWER to weigh rather than silently assumed sufficient.

Encountered and had to clean up significant environment contamination (stale tenant_template_build_* schemas across all 16 test databases) that caused a fully spurious 110-failure scripts/test_parallel.sh run, unrelated to this change. Root cause: tool-call-timeout kills of earlier stress-verification runs during this same session left template-clone builds interrupted mid-transaction. Not a new issue class (adjacent to ISS-0107's known Windows orphaned-process pattern) but this specific stale-build-schema flavor of it is not yet separately documented; ORCH/REVIEWER may want to fold a `tenant_template_build_*` sweep into the mandated pre-suite cleanup step alongside the existing `tenant_template` sweep, since the current mandated cleanup command in this run's own task brief only targets the bare `tenant_template` schema name, not its `_build_<hash>` transient variants.
